implementation_constraints: reads entire stdin once, writes single JSON array (or literal ERROR) to stdout, exits 0 in all paths
in-memory state (list + counter) scoped to one process run, no persistence

unresolved_intent.decision: treat only strings matching ^[1-9][0-9]*$ as a valid positive-integer id; reject '0', leading zeros ('007'), '+1', '-1', decimals, and empty segment as 404
unresolved_intent.rationale: spec says 'not a positive integer -> 404' but doesn't define canonical string form; rejecting non-canonical forms avoids ambiguity between id-as-string vs id-as-number

unresolved_intent.decision: validate the request body (400) before checking whether the item exists (404)
unresolved_intent.rationale: spec doesn't order these checks explicitly; body shape is a property of the request itself and is cheaper/more fundamental to validate first, independent of collection state

unresolved_intent.decision: compare 'method' field via exact case-sensitive string equality (e.g. 'GET', not 'get')
unresolved_intent.rationale: spec examples use uppercase method names and gives no case-folding rule; exact match is the least surprising default

unresolved_intent.decision: treat as undefined path -> 404, not as item route with empty id
unresolved_intent.rationale: spec doesn't mention trailing slashes; splitting yields an empty final segment which fails the single-non-empty-segment shape of '/items/<id>', so it falls into the general undefined-path 404 bucket alongside '/items/1/extra'
